cards.title: Synonyms, Antonyms, Analogies
rule: Definition: Vocabulary Relations and Semantic Matching (ስነ-ትርጉማዊ ዝምድናታትን ምትካእ ቃላትን) refers to the systems of identifying words with similar meanings (synonyms), opposite meanings (antonyms), proportional logical relationships (analogies), and single lexical terms that compress complex descriptive definitions (one-word substitutes).

In national matriculation examinations, vocabulary is heavily tested through context-based semantic matching. Words rarely possess absolute synonyms; instead, their closest semantic partner is determined entirely by the surrounding clausal syntax ($$\text{Word} \leftrightarrow \text{Contextual Synonym}$$). Academic English relies extensively on Greek and Latin roots (e.g., *mal-* [bad], *bene-* [good], *chron-* [time], *auto-* [self]). Contrast this with Tigrinya's Semitic root-and-pattern morphology, where related vocabulary is derived internally from consonantal roots (ሰለስተ-ፊደል ሱር). Because English utilizes concatenative foreign roots (e.g., *benevolent* $$\rightarrow$$ *well-wishing*), Tigrinya speakers must learn to dissect complex academic words into their constituent morphemes ($$\text{Prefix} + \text{Root} + \text{Suffix}$$) to deduce synonyms and antonyms without relying on rote memorization.

body: Definition: Vocabulary Relations and Semantic Matching (ስነ-ትርጉማዊ ዝምድናታትን ምትካእ ቃላትን) refers to the systems of identifying words with similar meanings (synonyms), opposite meanings (antonyms), proportional logical relationships (analogies), and single lexical terms that compress complex descriptive definitions (one-word substitutes).

In national matriculation examinations, vocabulary is heavily tested through context-based semantic matching. Words rarely possess absolute synonyms; instead, their closest semantic partner is determined entirely by the surrounding clausal syntax ($$\text{Word} \leftrightarrow \text{Contextual Synonym}$$). Academic English relies extensively on Greek and Latin roots (e.g., *mal-* [bad], *bene-* [good], *chron-* [time], *auto-* [self]). Contrast this with Tigrinya's Semitic root-and-pattern morphology, where related vocabulary is derived internally from consonantal roots (ሰለስተ-ፊደል ሱር). Because English utilizes concatenative foreign roots (e.g., *benevolent* $$\rightarrow$$ *well-wishing*), Tigrinya speakers must learn to dissect complex academic words into their constituent morphemes ($$\text{Prefix} + \text{Root} + \text{Suffix}$$) to deduce synonyms and antonyms without relying on rote memorization.

Antonyms (ኣንጻር ቃላት) are tested both as entirely distinct lexical items (e.g., *ephemeral* vs. *permanent*) and as morphological opposites formed via negative prefixes ($$\text{Root} \leftrightarrow \text{Prefix} + \text{Root}$$, e.g., *orthodox* vs. *unorthodox*, *compatible* vs. *incompatible*). In reading passages, contextual clues such as contrastive conjunctions (*however, although, on the other hand, whereas*) serve as semantic signposts pointing directly to the required antonymous meaning. Students must look for these structural transitions to accurately determine the opposite meaning of a highlighted word.

cards.title: Worked practice
cards.problem: The effects of the traditional medicine were ________, lasting only a few minutes before the pain returned.

steps.text: The context 'lasting only a few minutes' indicates that the effects were short-lived, requiring an adjective meaning temporary.
Students often confuse 'potent' (powerful) or 'inevitable' (unavoidable) with the correct option.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The effects of the traditional medicine were ________, lasting only a few minutes before the pain returned.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The context 'lasting only a few minutes' indicates that the effects were short-lived, requiring an adjective meaning temporary.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often confuse 'potent' (powerful) or 'inevitable' (unavoidable) with the correct option. 'Ephemeral' (Option B) is the precise academic synonym for short-lived.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'Ephemeral' (ሳሕቲ/ኣዝዩ ሕጽር ዝበለ ግዜ ዝጸንሕ) ዝብል ቃል፡ ንሓጺር እዋን ጥራይ ዝጸንሕ ኩነታት ንምግላጽ የገልግል። እቲ ሓረግ 'lasting only a few minutes' (ንሒደት ደቓይቕ ጥራይ ዝጸንሐ) ስለ ዝበለ፡ ቅኑዕ መልሲ Option B እዩ።

cards.title: Worked practice
cards.problem: Unlike his highly ________ predecessor, the new director was malevolent and treated the employees with cruelty.

steps.text: The contrastive conjunction 'Unlike' indicates that the blank must contain the antonym of 'malevolent' (evil-wishing/cruel).
Students must identify 'benevolent' (Option B - kind/well-wishing) as the exact antonym of 'malevolent'.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Unlike his highly ________ predecessor, the new director was malevolent and treated the employees with cruelty.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The contrastive conjunction 'Unlike' indicates that the blank must contain the antonym of 'malevolent' (evil-wishing/cruel).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students must identify 'benevolent' (Option B - kind/well-wishing) as the exact antonym of 'malevolent'. Both words share the root '-volent' (wishing), with 'bene-' (good) and 'male-' (bad) prefixes.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'Unlike' (ዘይከም) ዝብል ናይ መነጻጸሪ ቃል ስለ ዘሎ፡ እቲ ባዶ ቦታ ናይ 'malevolent' (እኩይ/ጨካን) ኣንጻር ቃል ክኸውን ኣለዎ። 'Benevolent' (ርሕሩሕ/ደግ) ምስቲ 'bene-' (ጽቡቕ) ዝብል ናይ ላቲን ሱር ዝተኣሳሰር ኮይኑ ቅኑዕ ኣንጻር ቃል እዩ (Option B)።

cards.title: Worked practice
cards.problem: Choose the option that correctly completes the analogy: **Carpenter : Saw :: Surgeon : ________**

steps.text: A carpenter uses a saw as his primary tool, in the same way that a surgeon uses a scalpel as his primary tool.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Choose the option that correctly completes the analogy: **Carpenter : Saw :: Surgeon : ________**
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The relationship is Worker-and-Tool ($$\text{Worker} : \text{Tool}$$). A carpenter uses a saw as his primary tool, in the same way that a surgeon uses a scalpel as his primary tool.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often choose 'Operation' (Option D) or 'Hospital' (Option B) because they are related to surgery, but they do not match the specific Worker-and-Tool logical relationship. Option C is correct.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
እዚ ናይ ስነ-ሞጎት ዝምድና 'ሰራሕተኛን መሳርሒኡን' (Worker-and-Tool) የርእየና። ጸራቢ ዕንጨይቲ (carpenter) ንመጋዝ (saw) ከም መሳርሒኡ ይጥቀመሉ፤ ከምኡ ውን ሓኪም መጥባሕቲ (surgeon) ንመጥባሕቲ መላጸ (scalpel) ከም መሳርሒኡ ይጥቀመሉ (Option C)።
